newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end lower, gold at 3 year low.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end lower, gold at 3 year low.

text.p: New York precious metals futures began the new year Thursday, as they ended last year - on a weak note.
Spot gold in the bullion market slid to a new three year low and life-of-contract lows were seen in nearby active gold and platinum futures.
"This could get worse before it gets better," Chase Manhattan New York managing director Dinsa Mehta said.
"The shorts still think they have all the protection they need from potential central bank sales, but gold equities are the most undervalued they have been in 16 months," he said.
COMEX February gold ended down $2.60 at $366.60 an ounce after falling to a life-of-contract low of $366.50, with April and June gold also posting contract lows.
Total estimated gold futures volume was 35,000 lots.
Spot gold in the bullion market ended quoted at $365.25/75 after a fix at a three-year low of $366.55 in London Thursday afternoon compared to Tuesday's New York close of $367.45/95.
"It looks like gold is breaking out of its range of the past month to the downside, led by more fund selling," Refco New York analyst Jim Steel said.

COMEX was closed Wednesday for the New Year holiday. Open interest data for Tuesday, released Thursday morning, showed a jump of 4,574 lots in February gold open interest to 93,044 lots, suggesting funds were adding to already large net short positions, analysts said.
The slump in the U.S. bond and stocks markets Thursday on a higher-than-expected December NAPM index failed to prompt investment flows in gold, traders said.

The December National Association of Purchasing Managers Index rose to 54.0 from 52.7 in November. A reading above 50 pct indicates an expansion in the manufacturing sector and the possibility of higher inflation.
The potential for further central bank gold sales in 1997 and soft physical demand was keeping sentiment bearish, analysts said.
COMEX March silver ended down 5.8 cents at $4.732 after setting a session low of $4.730, not far from the four-week low set Tuesday of $4.710. Total estimated silver futures volume was 14,000 lots.
The spot gold/silver ratio edged up to 77.52 Thursday, continuing the recovery from a three-month low of 75.46 set Dec 26.
NYMEX nearby active April platinum ended down $3.50 at $371.00 after falling to a life-of-contract low of $370.50, with January and July deliveries also setting contract lows.
The April gold/platinum spread slipped to $2.30 from $3.20 Tuesday.
NYMEX March palladium closed down $0.80 at $123.25, correcting from its runup Tuesday, after palladium fixed at a 15-week high at $120.75 in London Thursday morning.
